_comment: Facts the SAMAVESH Figma documentation pages assert about the code. Each entry pins one Figma TEXT node: `figma` is a snapshot of what it says, `expect` re-derives the same fact from the code. tools/figma-doc-parity/check.mjs fails when the two disagree. Every claim below was wrong on 2026-08-19 and is recorded here so it cannot rot again silently.

claims.where: AccessibilityBar — Documentation › 01 Anatomy › Government of India
claims.figma: Body/body-2 (14/20). Underlines on hover and focus only — on the words, not the launch glyph.

expect.hint: The bar's label type. Said Label/label-2 (12/16) until 2026-08-19, after the master had already moved to 14.
The underline is hover/focus-scoped and lives on the LABEL, not the anchor — otherwise text-decoration propagates onto the launch glyph.
There must be no RESTING underline — only :hover / :focus-visible on the label.

claims.figma: Launch glyph, 12 px.

expect.hint: Verified correct on 2026-08-19 — pinned so it stays that way.

claims.figma: text/neutral/inverse · Body/body-2

expect.hint: label-2 is 12px. The bar has been body-2 since the master moved to 14.

claims.figma: White label, 14 / 20.

expect.hint: The spacing ladder is VALUE-NAMED. inline/s, inline/m, inline/l, padding/m and padding/2xl no longer exist.
If the stylesheet stops using a rung listed here, this row is describing spacing the bar no longer has.

claims.figma: shape/2 · shape/4

expect.hint: Radius is value-named too; shape/xxs and shape/xs are dead names that rendered radius 0.

claims.figma: Divider · Vertical / Inverse subtle

expect.hint: The bar standardised on the quieter inverse rule on 2026-08-19.

claims.figma: WCAG 2.2 AA + GIGW

expect.hint: The estate targets 2.2 AA — see .claude/rules/standards-precedence.md. GIGW binds 2.1; 2.2 is a strict superset, so conforming to 2.2 satisfies it.

claims.figma: Every control is tabbable; focus renders inverse ink at 2px — never focus/ring (see 04).

expect.hint: This row said focus "uses focus/ring" until 2026-08-19, contradicting §04 on the same page. focus/ring is #0373DF and measures 1.37:1 on this bar's #005EB9 fill; inverse ink is 6.36:1.
If the bar ever starts using focus/ring, this claim — and the WCAG 1.4.11 conformance behind it — is void.

claims.figma: 14 px body
WCAG 2.2 · 2.5.8. Steppers are 24×24; the accessibility and language buttons 28×28, via transparent hit-area frames.

expect.hint: 2.5.8 Target Size (Minimum) is 24×24 at AA. 44×44 is 2.5.5 Enhanced (AAA) and is NOT claimed.

claims.figma: Samajik Sahayak

expect.hint: The seal has the name written round the ring, so the header says the same thing.
The panel title defaults to the name, not to an invitation.

This exact string sat in two JSDoc @default tags, in the props table on the web docs, in the Figma master and in this Identity panel long after the implementation moved on. Four surfaces agreed with each other and disagreed with the code.

claims.figma: Bot turns carry an avatar; user turns do not. Bubbles cap at 67% so the column never reads as a wall of text. Suggestions wrap and pack RIGHT, on the user’s side — each is a sentence they are about to say.

expect.hint: Suggestions sit on the user's side because pressing one becomes a user bubble, which lands hard right.
Without this the docs page's own `.ds-prose li + li` margin offsets every pill after the first by 8px.

claims.figma: The mascot at 40px, the bilingual title block, then start over (restart_alt), expand (open_in_full) and minimise (close) as 32px targets, in that order — ✕ last, because the top-right corner is where every user reaches to dismiss. Every glyph is a Material Symbols Rounded instance, never a drawn path. The row gap is 8, not 12: at 12 the third control left the brand 125px for a title needing 128, and “Samajik Sahayak” wrapped onto two lines.

expect.hint: Start over, then expand, then ✕ LAST. The top-right corner is where people reach to dismiss and nothing may take that slot.

8, not 12. With three controls the brand had 125px for a title needing 128 — a three-pixel shortfall, enough to wrap the title onto two lines. Pinned in e2e/chatbot/end-chat.spec.ts as well, because it breaks silently.

claims.figma: A pill composer and the honest note, at the full width of the panel — and nothing else. Start over lived here through THREE arrangements and each broke something measurable: hard right put it 25px under Send in the same 32px column; at the head of the note’s row its 101px pushed the disclaimer 109px off the panel’s left edge and rewrapped it to three lines; on its own line it added 24px of height to a panel already tight on a phone. It is a HEADER control now, with expand and close. The footer is where the citizen SAYS things; a panel-level reset is not something they say.

expect.hint: The footer block holds the note and NOTHING else. Three arrangements put Start over in here and each broke something measurable — Send's column, the panel's left edge, 24px of height on a phone.

Start over is the HEADER's own icon button, matching expand and minimise. It was a DS Button while it lived in the footer, which was right there and would be wrong here: three icons in one corner must match.

claims.figma: width 400, height 719 (a CAP, not a fixed height — the panel sizes to its content), launcher 84, bubbleMax 246, typingDot 5. Bound to the frames here and resolved by chatbot.css there, so neither side can move alone.

expect.hint: The library carried 6 while the master and the stylesheet both drew 5, because nothing was bound to it.
The stylesheet must RESOLVE these, not restate the numbers.
719 is the ceiling. Pinned there as a height, the opening state was 435px of white under the header — about 45% of the panel.

claims.figma: 32, 40 and 48px. All three clear the 24x24 WCAG 2.2 (2.5.8) Level AA minimum. 44x44 is 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), Level AAA — only lg reaches it, and UX4G 3.0 recommends it on mobile along with 8px between adjacent targets. Treat 44 as a touch-context recommendation, never as a WCAG failure on a pointer surface.

expect.hint: sm is 32px. This page said sm 'meets the 44px height requirement' in three places, including inside the accessibility checklist, until 2026-08-25. The regex names min-height deliberately: `height: 32px` also matches `min-height: 32px`, so the looser pattern would keep passing if the fix were ever reverted.
lg is the only size reaching 44.

claims.where: Button — Documentation › 03 Size › How it scales
claims.figma: The height is a MINIMUM, not a fixed height. Each size sets min-height plus vertical padding, so the box grows with the text instead of clipping it: at 200% an md button used to hold 40px while its content needed 41. min-height is what makes a button 32/40/48 at 100%; the padding stays under that and becomes the breathing room as the text scales. WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text.

expect.hint: md is a minimum. Reverting to a fixed `height` reintroduces the 1.4.4 clipping this section describes.

NO bare `height` in any of the three SIZE rules — the assertion that actually holds the fix, since a min-height on md means nothing if sm or lg quietly keeps a fixed one. Two corrections on 2026-08-27: it was `^\s+height:` over the whole file, which fired on the busy spinner's legitimate `height: 1em`; and the first narrowing excluded `min-` but not `line-`, so it matched the size rules' own `line-height`. Both lookbehinds are load-bearing.
The vertical padding is half the fix. Without it min-height alone still centres a clipped label.

claims.figma: Default, hover, pressed, focused and disabled are drawn here as variants so a designer can see them. In CODE there is no state prop — CSS drives hover, active and disabled. Never add one. Loading IS a prop as of 2026-08-27: loading sets aria-busy and disables the control, but it deliberately does not swap the label — pass “Submitting…” yourself.

expect.hint: State is a Figma variant axis only. A state prop in code would be the drift this line exists to prevent.
The loading prop exists. This page claimed the component set aria-busy, then that it had no loading state at all; it now has one and says so.
Busy implies disabled. A button that says “Submitting…” and still submits is the double-submission this prop exists to prevent.

claims.where: SAMAVESH Banner — Documentation › 07 Tokens › What the masthead publishes
claims.figma: --sa-header-stuck is the header's CURRENT pinned height and exists only on sticky headers. --sa-header-bottom is where the header ends right now. The distinction is the whole fix: the gap was about WHICH variable, never about when the band pins.

expect.hint: The masthead must PUBLISH the pinned height. Reading the resting height instead is what put a gap between header and band.
The band's sticky `top` must RESOLVE the published value, never restate a header height. The header has three.

claims.where: SAMAVESH Banner — Documentation › 02 Closing › A POINTER LANDS OUTSIDE
claims.figma: pointerdown

expect.hint: Clicking empty space moves focus to <body> with a null relatedTarget, indistinguishable from a tab switch — so focusout alone cannot release the parked band.
The guard is load-bearing, not defensive styling: band.contains(window) THROWS, and a listener that throws leaves the band parked forever with no error anyone sees.

claims.figma: homepage_only

expect.hint: The band is an entry point: it earns its height where a reader is deciding where to go. Defaulting to "all" put it on every page.

claims.figma: No shadow

expect.hint: The resting card carries NO shadow. The colon is load-bearing: the base rule names box-shadow in its `transition` list as a property to ANIMATE, and a pattern without the colon matches that and reports a shadow the card does not have. It already has a saffron rule doing the separating — a shadow under a border is two boundary treatments for one edge, and if every card is elevated then elevation says nothing.
Press REMOVES the shadow. That is what makes it read as going down rather than merely shrinking.

claims.where: Portal Card — Documentation › 05 Do & Don't › href is required
claims.figma: It is required

expect.hint: REQUIRED, not optional. An optional destination rendered an unbuilt portal as a link and shipped a 404 on every page of the website; a required prop makes that a build error rather than a runtime one.
If href ever becomes optional again, this claim and the guarantee behind it are void.

claims.figma: When you have the slug rather than the route. An explicit slug BEATS a derived path.

expect.hint: Precedence, fixed 2026-08-31. PortalCard passes path={path ?? href} and href is REQUIRED, so under the old `path !== undefined` test the org branch was unreachable — every card carrying an org silently rendered the State Emblem.
The old precedence. Restoring it re-breaks every external card's mark.

claims.figma: One variant each, plus an Emblem variant for the fallback — 18 in all, mirroring ORG_LOGOS and ORG_LOGO_FALLBACK.

expect.hint: 17 organisations in ORG_LOGOS plus ORG_LOGO_FALLBACK, against 18 library variants — 17 orgs plus Emblem. The fallback is deliberately NOT one of the seventeen.
The page said 'Sixteen marks' in its header while its own body said seventeen — it contradicted itself until 2026-08-31.
e-Anudaan and e-Utthaan must NOT be in PORTAL_ORG_LOGOS — they resolve through the fallback to the State Emblem, which is what the library's Emblem variant now draws for them.

claims.figma: Device (2) × Auth Method (4) — Password, OTP, PIN and NGO-DARPAN ID.

expect.hint: The Figma Auth Method axis maps 1:1 onto these four. A fifth value in the enum means the master needs a fifth variant, or the enum is wrong.
Reinstated 2026-09-03. The master now carries Device × Auth Method = 8 variants including DARPAN, so code and Figma agree again.

expect.value: Password, OTP, PIN and NGO-DARPAN ID

claims.figma: variant → no code prop. Desktop is 1440 × 960 and Mobile 375 × 1138, where 1138 is the scroll height rather than a viewport. The React component is responsive in CSS, so the axis exists only to pin a breakpoint on the canvas. Tablet uses the Mobile variant by decision.

expect.hint: Device is DELIBERATELY not a prop. Adding one would give a designer two ways to say the same thing and let them disagree.
The Code Connect template must keep saying why Device has no prop, or an agent reading Dev Mode will invent one.

claims.figma: enum → the active role's defaultMode: password | otp | pin. Changes the form card only. DigiLocker is not a value here — it is an identity handoff above the credentials divider, switched by Show DigiLocker on Auth / AuthFormCard.

expect.hint: The variant pins a method on the canvas; the live value is the component's own state, seeded from the active role's defaultMode.

expect.pattern: DIGILOCKER IS NOT AN AUTH METHOD
expect.hint: Giving DigiLocker a variant is the mistake this line exists to prevent — it is a consent handoff, not a credential form.

claims.figma: Six variants ship: two devices by three authentication methods. The role and the selector style ride on nested instances, so the three specimens below are all reachable without adding a single variant.

expect.hint: The set was re-cut in place from Device × Step = 8 to Device × Auth Method = 6. If that arithmetic changes, this section's three specimens and its title change with it.

claims.figma: shape/12 · padding/24 · stack/16

expect.hint: Both ladders are value-named, so the rung IS the pixel value. A rung that stops resolving to its own name is the defect space-linkage.test.mjs exists to catch.
shape/lg, padding/xl and stack/m are DEAD names from before the value-naming migration. This node carried all three until 2026-09-02.

claims.figma: The PIN field takes digits only and renders masked. Its reveal control is PasswordInput's, not a hand-rolled one — the template drew its own Show/Hide button until 2026-09-03. Recovery is Forgot PIN rather than a password link, because a portal that signs in on a PIN has no password to reset.

expect.hint: Digits only — the field also strips non-digits on change, so a pasted value cannot smuggle letters in.
A PIN portal has no password to reset, so the recovery link must not be the password one.

The masked field's reveal control belongs to PasswordInput. It was hand-rolled here with its own Show/Hide button and its own aria-label, which is how one field ends up behaving unlike every other password field in the estate.

claims.figma: DigiLocker is an identity handoff, not a form mode, so it has no variant. Its card sits above the credentials divider and is switched by Show DigiLocker on the form card. It is offered per role rather than per audience: the handoff carries it on Citizen and on neither Admin nor Garima Greh. The divider appears only with the card.

expect.hint: The real gate. This assertion used to match the WORD "audience" in a types.ts COMMENT, which made the claim circular — the documentation was pinned to prose restating it rather than to code doing it.
Per role, not per audience. The handoff hides the card for officer AND organisation, so an audience rule would have been wrong in both directions.
"Not a form mode" pinned to the union it must stay out of. While it was a member, the template drew it as a fourth login method and suppressed the submit button behind it.
Written in the Code Connect template because it is the instruction an agent reading Dev Mode needs and cannot infer from geometry.

claims.figma: Put the portal's roles, authModes, authSelectorType and defaultMode in a login-config.ts beside the page.

expect.hint: The page named a prop `authModeOptions` that is a different, optional field. A reader copying the wrong name gets a config that silently offers no methods.

claims.figma: Focus is never obscured by the sticky masthead (2.4.11), and every control clears the 24 × 24 minimum (2.5.8). The security check is off unless a role asks for it — it resolves role.captcha, then config.captcha, then off — and when it is on it renders BotCheck, which is invisible by default and never a cognitive function test. 3.3.8 Accessible Authentication forbids one without an alternative, so a check renders only where a route out is also configured.

expect.hint: The check renders only where a ROLE opts in, with the portal as a fallback. `??` and not `||`, so a role's explicit false opts OUT of a portal-wide default rather than being read as unset. Flipping the final term to true would put a check on every login in the estate.
The reason for the default must stay beside the prop, or the next person removes the default as an inconvenience.
44 × 44 is 2.5.5 Target Size (Enhanced), Level AAA, which this estate does not claim. The AA minimum is 24 × 24 — see standards-precedence.md.
BOTH halves required. A bot check with nowhere for a blocked citizen to go has no accessible alternative at all, so a portal that switches one on without a route gets nothing rather than a dead end.

claims.figma: Maps Device and Auth Method onto the React props and carries the rules a snippet cannot show. Published from the repo root with npm run figma:connect; npm run check:code-connect gates drift.

expect.hint: The include glob in figma.config.json is root-relative, so running this from a workspace silently publishes nothing. The page must keep saying 'from the repo root'.
The page claimed Code Connect needed a Developer seat this estate did not have. @figma/code-connect v2 is installed and the templates resolve; only publishing needs the token.
45 = Size 3 x Checked 3 x State 5; the fixture records every axis. If an axis grows or shrinks, this number is wrong.

All twelve control/selection/* declarations, in ladder order: size, glyph and dot at sm/md/lg, then border/width, radius and gap. A thirteenth would make the hero's 12 a lie; this pattern only proves the twelve exist, so count when adding one.
2px, up from a raw 1.5px; aliases border.width.md.

expect.pattern: has no raw px outside comments
expect.hint: The stylesheet test fails the build on any raw px or duration in the selection stylesheets.

claims.figma: The hit area is 24 at sm, 44 at md, 48 at lg, measured in the browser. The default meets the AA minimum without its label and UX4G's 44×44 touch recommendation.

expect.hint: md rows take target/comfortable (44); sm target/min (24); lg target/spacious (48).

claims.where: Checkbox — Documentation › 05 Accessibility › 1.4.11 Contrast and focus
claims.figma: A 2px edge in border/neutral/base, 7.16:1 on white. The focus ring is a solid outline in focus/ring, painted in Highlight under forced colours, where the checked fill is also painted. selection-css.test.ts.

expect.hint: The ratio is measured at build time into border/neutral/base's Figma description; if the rung moves, the measured ratio moves and this claim fails.
The checked fill is painted in the system colour under forced colours.
30 = Size 3 x Checked 2 x State 5.
20 = Control 2 x Checked 2 x State 5.
4 = Orientation 2 x Layout 2.

claims.figma: The hit area is 24 at sm, 44 at md, 48 at lg; the card stretches the input to the tile's edges. The default meets the AA minimum without its label.

expect.hint: On the card the input stretches to the tile's edges.

claims.where: Radio — Documentation › 05 Accessibility › 1.4.11 Contrast and focus
claims.figma: A 2px edge in border/neutral/base, 7.16:1 on white; the dot is bg/brand/primary/bolder. The focus ring is a solid outline in focus/ring; under forced colours the selected edge and dot are painted in Highlight.

expect.hint: The ratio is measured at build time into border/neutral/base's Figma description; if the rung moves, the measured ratio moves and this claim fails.
The dot is painted in the system colour under forced colours.
20 = Control 2 x Checked 2 x State 5.
Six non-variant properties before the three axes: Icon, Title, Description, Invalid, Show Icon, Show Description.

claims.where: Selection Card — Documentation › hero › 44px minimum target

expect.hint: The tile's minimum height is the comfortable target.
Every card in the estate binds cmp/card/radius.

claims.where: Selection Card — Documentation › hero › 0 raw values

expect.pattern: has no raw px outside comments

tokenTables._comment: Every --sa-* a component's WEB documentation page names in its token table must be referenced by that component's stylesheet — or declared in `via` as reached through another component.
